message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the safety and order in mind.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Use a PC build checklist or a site like PCPartPicker to check compatibility. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access the interior. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Place it in the bottom rear (or top, depending on case). Secure with screws. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other parts. | Align standoffs, screw in, then attach I/O shield. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | If cooler has pre‑applied paste, skip step 9. Otherwise, apply a pea‑size amount. Attach cooler, secure. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Snap sticks into DIMM slots; ensure they click. |
|10 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
|11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual output & gaming. | Insert into the top PCIe x16 slot, secure with screws, connect any required PCIe power cables. |
|12 | **Connect Motherboard Power** | 24‑pin ATX + 8‑pin EPS. | Plug PSU cables into motherboard headers. |
|13 | **Connect Peripheral Power** | Fans, drives, front panel connectors. | Connect 4‑pin SATA power to drives, 4‑pin fan headers, front panel connectors (USB, audio, power button). |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Keeps airflow and looks tidy. | Use zip ties, Velcro straps, and route cables behind the motherboard tray. |
|15 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Prevent hardware damage. | Verify all cables are firmly seated, no loose screws. |
|16 | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panels, secure screws. |
|17 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Confirm hardware is recognized. | Power on, enter BIOS (usually F2, DEL, or ESC). Check CPU, RAM, storage detection. |
|18 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB flash drive with Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc. Follow on‑screen instructions. |
|19 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure optimal performance. | Download motherboard chipset drivers, GPU drivers, Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth drivers. |
|20 | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify stability and performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) and benchmarks (Cinebench, 3DMark). |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **Case** – ATX, mATX, or ITX, with good airflow.
- **Motherboard** – Socket matches CPU, enough PCIe slots, enough RAM slots.
- **CPU** – Core count, clock speed, integrated graphics (if needed).
- **GPU** – VRAM, power connectors, size fits case.
- **RAM** – DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity.
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD for OS, SATA SSD/HDD for bulk.
- **PSU** – Wattage ≥ 80+ Bronze, modular if you want cleaner cables.
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, or AIO liquid cooler.
- **Operating System** – Windows, Linux, or others.

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; never touch metal contacts while components are powered. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, use quality thermal paste, keep dust out. |
| **Component incompatibility** | Double‑check socket, BIOS version, PSU wattage before buying. |
| **Cable clutter** | Plan cable routes early; use zip ties. |
| **Boot failure** | Verify all power connectors, check BIOS for missing devices. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Forums** – r/buildapc on Reddit, Tom’s Hardware.  

Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
